elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: Rendered 9.9(a): "Such audit shall not occur more than once in a given Calendar Year", and the open-ended "unless for cause" carve-out has been deleted; Calendar Year is defined (1.11) as a successive 12-month period, so the cap operates on a 12-month basis. The deterministic check "audit frequency limited" reports false, but on inspection of the operative text the frequency is expressly capped at one audit per Calendar Year, so the regex appears to be a wording mismatch (it does not search for "once in a given Calendar Year") rather than a substantive gap.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 30 days' written notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Rendered 9.9(a) requires only "at least fifteen (15) days' prior notice"; to meet the preferred element the operative text must read at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice (the current text also says "prior notice", not "written notice").
No business-hours limitation appears anywhere in rendered 9.9(a), (c) or (d); the drafter expressly declined to press it.

elements.element: Audits are conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: Rendered 9.9(a): "permit an independent auditor of international prominence, selected by the auditing Party and reasonably acceptable to the audited Party, to audit the books and records".

elements.element: The auditor is bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: Rendered 9.9(d): "the Parties shall cause the auditor to enter into a reasonably acceptable confidentiality agreement with the audited Party obligating such auditor to retain all such financial information in confidence".

elements.element: Audits are conducted off-site where possible.
elements.evidence: No off-site or location language in the rendered clause; the audit of "books and records maintained pursuant to Section 9.8" is silent as to venue, so the element would require an express insertion.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Rendered 9.9(c) shifts cost where the underpayment "was more than ten percent (10%)", not 5 percent.

elements.element: Vendor has no direct access to Customer systems for an audit.
elements.evidence: No express prohibition on access to Customer systems was inserted; the clause only scopes the audit to "books and records maintained pursuant to Section 9.8", which is an implied limit, not the express no-systems-access statement the element requires.

elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: Rendered 9.9(a): "Such audit shall not occur more than once in a given Calendar Year"; the blank "[***] in a given Calendar Year" is filled and the "unless for cause" exception (which would have defeated any cap) is deleted, so the once-per-year limit is now effective and reciprocal.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Rendered 9.9(a): "but in any event at least fifteen (15) days' prior notice", replacing the blank "[***] prior notice".

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent.
elements.evidence: Rendered 9.9(c): "The auditing Party shall bear the full cost of such audit unless such audit reveals an underpayment ... more than ten percent (10%) of the amount set forth in such report"; as the clause is mutual, Vendor as auditing Party bears cost unless the 10% threshold is exceeded.

reasons: Fallback is complete: all three parametric blanks (frequency, notice, cost-shift trigger) are filled in operative language at or better than the fallback thresholds, and no element is left to the margin comment.

Preferred is not complete: notice is 15 rather than 30 days, the cost-shift trigger is 10% rather than 5%, and there is no business-hours, off-site or no-systems-access language. Independent auditor and auditor confidentiality (9.9(a) and (d)) are already met and correctly left untouched.

The deterministic "audit frequency limited" check returns false, but substantive inspection of the rendered text shows an express cap ("shall not occur more than once in a given Calendar Year") with the for-cause escape removed; the failure is a pattern mismatch, not a drafting gap. No repair is required.

Minimality holds: only the three fallback parameters were changed, plus deletion of "unless for cause", which is necessary because an open-ended for-cause exception would defeat the once-per-year element. The unrelated blanks in the look-back/waiver sentence ([***] preceding Calendar Years) were correctly left intact, and no extras (business hours, off-site, systems-access, survival, expense or procedural language) were added.

Intent is preserved: the audit right remains mutual, the scope (books and records under Section 9.8), the auditor-selection mechanic, the look-back and waiver sentence, and the Article XI confidentiality overlay all survive without contradiction; no defined term or cross-reference is left dangling.

Classification as a deviation is supportable: before the edit the frequency, notice and cost-shift figures were all redacted blanks, so the clause failed the fallback on material terms and had no effective frequency cap.
